topic.label: German Studies
topic.desc: German Studies: the German language and the literatures, thought, history and cultures of the German-speaking countries.

concepts: German morphology and syntax: cases, declension, verb position, separable verbs, modal verbs and the subjunctive.
Translating between German and English and describing German phonology, dialects and language history.
Literature in German from the Middle Ages through Sturm und Drang, classicism, romanticism, realism and modernism to the present.
German intellectual traditions from Kant, Hegel, Marx and Nietzsche to the Frankfurt School and beyond.
The German-speaking lands from the Holy Roman Empire through unification, the world wars, National Socialism, division and reunification.
Film, media, politics and society in Germany, Austria and Switzerland today.
skills: Generates article and adjective endings across nominative, accusative, dative and genitive and checks each against declension tables.
Corrects verb-second, verb-final and separable verb placement in learner sentences and checks each fix with the rule.
Builds Konjunktiv I and II sentences for reported speech and hypotheticals and checks forms against conjugation tables.
Translates passages between German and English with DeepL and checks meaning, compounds and false friends.
Splits German compound nouns into components with linking elements and checks the gender rule of the head noun.
Describes features of a German dialect or national variety such as Swiss or Austrian German and checks examples against documented usage.
Produces a close reading of a German poem or prose passage and checks every interpretive claim is anchored in a quotation.
Profiles a period such as Weimar classicism or Romanticism with authors, works and aesthetics and checks dates and attributions.
Searches peer-reviewed German studies scholarship through Wiley Scholar Gateway and checks each citation resolves to the stated work.
Explains a concept such as Aufklarung or Dialektik in its original context and checks the account against the primary text.
Reconstructs a philosophical argument from a German text as premises and conclusion and checks validity.
Applies a Frankfurt School concept such as the culture industry to a cultural object and checks fidelity to the source text.
Evaluates a German historical document for author, audience and context and checks claims against corroborating sources.
Builds a dated chronology of a period such as the Weimar Republic and checks each date against reference works.
Analyses Vergangenheitsbewaltigung and commemoration practices and checks examples against documented memorials and debates.
Analyses a German-language film from Expressionism to the Berlin School in its historical context and checks claims against the film and sources.
Explains a feature of contemporary German, Austrian or Swiss society and checks factual claims against official sources.
Builds comprehension questions on German-language news and checks that answers are supported by the source.
mcp: Translate text and documents across 100+ languages, with your preferred styles applied
Enhance responses with scholarly research and citations
